claims.text: As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
HfNbTaTiZr has inadequate oxidation resistance for high-temperature use in air.
The poor oxygen resistance of untreated HfNbTaTiZr causes deep oxygen ingress.
The poor oxygen resistance of untreated HfNbTaTiZr causes embrittlement under high-temperature oxidative conditions.
Pre-oxidation at 600–700 °C under low oxygen partial pressure for about one hour will form a thin HfO2 surface layer on HfNbTaTiZr.
The pre-formed HfO2 layer will be continuous, uniform, and adherent.
A continuous HfO2 scale acts as an oxygen-diffusion barrier at temperatures up to 1000 °C.
The HfO2 scale will passivate the alloy surface and limit oxygen ingress during high-temperature exposure in air.
Limiting oxygen ingress will prevent deep oxidation of the subsurface region.
The surface treatment will preserve the as-cast bulk microstructure.
Pre-oxidized specimens will have significantly less oxidation depth than untreated specimens after prolonged exposure at up to 1000 °C in an oxidizing atmosphere.
Pre-oxidized specimens will exhibit less oxidation-induced embrittlement than untreated specimens under high-temperature tensile stress.
Pre-oxidized specimens will retain yield strength comparable to untreated specimens under tensile loading at strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
Pre-oxidized specimens will retain ductility comparable to untreated specimens under tensile loading at strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
The treatment remains effective only while the HfO2 scale remains stable and adherent during high-temperature tensile loading.
